title: BlueCedar claims edge deployment — probe notes
content:
Context:
- Pre-sales > pilot phase. BlueCedar is a mid-size claims processor (insurer B2B) evaluating our Private (VPC/on-prem) option and an edge component for regional processing. They want deterministic latency for first-pass triage (NLP extraction + triage scoring) at multiple regional data centers.
- Call with BlueCedar infra + platform + NLP lead 2025-10-02 (45m). Notes below are raw, action-focused — for Marco/Darnell/Aisha to iterate into proposal draft.

Attendees:
- BlueCedar: Priya Anand (Platform), Tomas Li (NLP lead), Omar Haddad (Security), Elaine Park (SRE)
- Redwood: Sofia Chen (SE, owner), Marco Ruiz (infra), Darnell Price (private-deploy lead)

High-level ask (what they said):
- Low and predictable 95th percentile latency for short inference requests (50-150 tokens): target P95 < 120ms within region.
- Data residency: EU + US regional tenancy. Some PII must never leave customer VPC.
- Offline fallback: if private capacity not available, fall back to hosted sandbox (but only with anonymized payloads).
- Integration: input stream from Kafka (regional clusters) -> preprocessing -> call Redwood runtime -> push results to internal event bus.

Key technical constraints (their infra):
- Kubernetes clusters in each region (EKS in us-west-2, GKE in europe-west1).
- Limited GPU quota initially: 2x A10g equivalents per region for pilot.
- They run strict egress rules; outbound to hosted services requires allowlist & static IPs.
- KMS: They use Azure Key Vault and expect us to integrate or allow customers to bring KMS/HSM for model keys and secrets.
- Storage for model artifacts must be internal S3-compatible (MinIO) — no external public buckets.

Immediate technical unknowns / follow-ups we promised:
- Exact tokenization profile: Tomas will share sample distribution (short triage prompts ~60 tokens median, 95th at ~220 tokens). TODO: get sample prompt set by 2025-10-06.
- Acceptable privacy redaction for fallback: legal to confirm what fields can be pseudonymized before leaving VPC.
- Expected QPS per region for pilot: Priya to confirm but ballpark 80–150 rps. We need to size batching/replicas accordingly.

Preliminary architecture suggestion (notes):
- Private control plane + on-prem runtime in each region (Redwood Private).
- Small dedicated pool per region with autoscale disabled for pilot (predictability) -> manual burst policy to central reserved cluster if needed.
- Keep a quantized variant for edge nodes (int8/4) to fit within 2x A10g constraint; do quality check on a sample eval set.
- Use local prefix/KV caching for repeated claims context to reduce tokens for follow-ups.
- Network egress: either configure static egress NAT IPs on their VPC or recommend an allowed proxy in-front of outbound calls for fallback sandbox traffic.

Gotchas / risk flags called out on the call:
- Latency target may be optimistic for A10g-equivalent with heavy NER + structured extraction model; we need to benchmark with their prompt set.
- KV cache hit rates unknown — if low, cost/latency will spike. Need sample workload and trace.
- KMS integration timeline: Azure Key Vault integration could add 4–6 weeks if certificate exchange + policy review required.
- Egress policy: customer legal may block any fallback that leaves VPC; fallback plan might be non-starter until legal signs off.
- Kafka connector complexity: they want at-least-once semantics; we need idempotency guidance for downstream events if a runtime restarts during processing.

Measurements & experiments to run (next week):
- Run local perf tests with their sample prompts: target P50/P95 latency and cost per 1k tokens. (Owner: Marco)
- Evaluate quantized model accuracy delta vs FP16 on bluecedar triage dataset (Owner: Darnell)
- Simulate KV cache hit patterns using 48-hour trace sample (Owner: Sofia)

Action items (who/when):
- Tomas: send sample prompt set + 48hr event trace (by 2025-10-06)
- Priya: QPS estimate and allowed egress list process owner (by 2025-10-07)
- Sofia: perf run plan + test harness to run on A10g. Need to align benchmark infra (by 2025-10-08)
- Marco: draft network egress options and static IP NAT approach; get list of required firewall ports we will need (by 2025-10-09)
- Darnell: quick accuracy checklist for quantized variant; pick two candidate models to test (by 2025-10-09)

Customer concerns to surface to product/security teams:
- Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK) completeness: they expect granular key usage logs and HSM-level attestation. Need to confirm HSM support on private package.
- SLA expectations vs pilot resources: they asked about P95 SLA for Dedicated vs Private. Clarify what we can promise in pilot (we likely cannot commit SLA until we have dedicated capacity).
- Rollout policy for fallback: they want automatic fallback but with policy controls that prevent sending PII to hosted; product should expose fine-grained fallback rules per field/route.

Notes-to-self (rough):
- When running perf, mimic their kafka payload + local preprocessing to get realistic tokens. Avoid synthetic prompts that inflate cache hits.
- For quantization check, include 50 labelled claims and evaluate extraction F1 for critical fields (policy number, date-of-loss, claimant name).
- Prepare a short one-pager for legal on privacy-preserving fallbacks: options = field-level pseudonymization, differential privacy, or local-only mode.

Next meeting: 2025-10-14 proposed (internal sync 2025-10-10 for Redwood team).

Misc scribbles / fragments:
- Cost concern: 2 A10gs @ scale ~? estimate tokens/rps -> monthly run-rate for pilot — build quick calc once QPS confirmed.
- Consider recommending canary model variants: smaller extractor for first pass + larger fallback for ambiguous cases. Could reduce GPU load.

End of raw notes.

(versioning: convert into customer-facing pilot plan doc once we have prompt/payload samples; expected draft by 2025-10-13).
